## Natural history notes

A native perennial herb in the yellow-eyed grass family, characterized by narrow, grass-like basal leaves and slender flowering stalks topped with small yellow flowers emerging from compact, cone-like heads. Fringed Yellow-eyed Grass occurs primarily in wet, acidic habitats such as depression marshes, wet savannas, boggy flats, and other seasonally saturated sites. In Florida it is most frequent in the northern and central parts of the state and becomes much rarer farther south, where it is considered critically imperiled. It is associated with open, fire-maintained wetlands and can decline where drainage, woody encroachment, or fire suppression alter these habitats.
